facts.statement: Cimolopteryx is a prehistoric bird genus that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Cimolopteryx (meaning "Cretaceous wing") is a prehistoric bird genus from the Late Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: Cimolopteryx was a small bird, roughly the size of a small gull.
facts.quote: Cimolopteryx was a fairly small bird, with a maximum size about equal to that of a small gull.

facts.statement: The genus is known almost exclusively from coracoid bones, which are part of the shoulder girdle.
facts.quote: It is known almost exclusively from a number of coracoids (a bone in the shoulder girdle).

facts.statement: Paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh first mentioned and informally named the first coracoid specimen in 1889, but did not validly describe it until 1892.
facts.quote: The first such coracoid to be found (specimen number YMP 1845, in the collections of the Peabody Museum of Natural History) was first mentioned and informally named by paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in the footnote of an 1889 paper, but it was not validly described by him until 1892.

facts.statement: The only specimen confidently attributed to Cimolopteryx rara was found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming and dates to the end of the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: The only specimen confidently attributed to C. rara was found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming, dating to the end of the Maastrichtian age, which ended about million years ago.

facts.statement: Federico Agnolin concluded that Cimolopteryx, Lamarqueavis, and Ceramornis could be grouped into the distinct family Cimolopterygidae based on coracoid bone similarities.
facts.quote: Agnolin looked at anatomical similarities between the various species' coracoid bones, and concluded that Cimolopteryx and Lamarqueavis could be grouped together, along with Ceramornis, in a distinct family, the Cimolopterygidae.

facts.statement: Cimolopteryx lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether multiple species of Cimolopteryx are distinct; Nicholas Longrich initially synonymized them in 2009 but reversed his position in 2011, considering them distinct.
facts.quote: In a 2009 review, Nicholas Longrich synonymized them as the same species, dismissing the size difference as possibly based on sex or growth stage. However, Longrich reversed his position following a 2011 analysis of Lancian birds, in which he and co-authors considered all four named species to be distinct.

facts.statement: In 2010, Federico Agnolin transferred Cimolopteryx minima and C. petra to the new genus Lamarqueavis due to their similarity to the South American species Lamarqueavis australis.
facts.quote: C. minima and C. petra were transferred to the new genus Lamarqueavis by Federico Agnolin in 2010, based on their similarity to the South American species L. australis.

rejected.statement: Sylvia Hope regarded Cimolopteryx as a likely member of the modern bird group Charadriiformes, which includes shorebirds.
rejected.quote: Hope regarded Cimolopteryx as a likely member of the modern bird group Charadriiformes, which includes a diverse array of shorebirds.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'as a likely member of the modern bird'

rejected.statement: Cimolopteryx maxima was about twice the size of C. rara, but its anatomy is insufficient to confirm if it belongs to the genus or represents a different genus.
rejected.quote: "Cimolopteryx" maxima was about twice the size of C. rara, but not enough of its anatomy is known to confidently determine if it belongs to Cimolopteryx or a different genus.
